title: Haunted Alabama: Paranormal investigation explores ghostly activity at Birmingham's Arlington House
excerpt: A paranormal investigation at the historic Arlington House in Birmingham’s Elyton neighborhood uncovered ghostly encounters, including sightings of a child spirit named Mary and evidence of Civil War-era soldiers.
content:
Haunted Alabama: Paranormal investigation explores ghostly activity at Birmingham’s Arlington House

BIRMINGHAM, Ala. —

A paranormal investigation at the historic Arlington House in Birmingham’s Elyton neighborhood revealed ghostly activity, including encounters with spirits tied to the home’s Civil War history and its former residents.

“All the equipment was going off. Sometimes the equipment does not even go off, but this place is definitely haunted,” said Lesley Ann Hyde of the Southern Ghost Girls, who has been investigating haunted locations for nearly a decade.

Hyde frequently brings her team to the Arlington House, where she said paranormal activity is almost guaranteed. “This is one of the most haunted places actually in Alabama,” she said.

During the investigation, participants reported seeing faces on gravestones, mysterious writing on windows, and paranormal equipment responding to spirits attempting to share their stories.

“The most prevalent ghost here that we feel is a child. If any of you have told me that you saw a blond-headed little girl, you probably saw Mary. Mary has known to haunt here,” Hyde said.

Mary is believed to be the daughter of Judge William Mudd, who purchased the house in 1842, two decades after it was built. Mudd’s connection to the Civil War adds to the mansion’s mysterious history.

“This was actually a very historic place during the Civil War. The Union soldiers under General Wilson, they actually marched into Arlington Historic House and they took it over. So there were 13,000 Union troops that were stationed here at Arlington,” Hyde said.

Hyde added, “We sometimes have ghosts of soldiers coming through.”

The investigation also revealed that multiple spirits can be present at the same time. “It’s very normal for there to be several spirits at one time. We’ve had up to ten at a time,” Hyde said.

Mark Travis of the Southern Ghost Girls echoed this sentiment. “Oh tons. It really depends on the energy of the people that come to the event,” Travis said.

The paranormal activity isn’t limited to the house itself. Travis shared that a former Birmingham mayor, who loved the Arlington House, requested his ashes be buried on the property.

Photographic evidence from the investigation revealed ghostly faces in statues, leaving participants stunned.

Whether it’s the harvest moon or something more sinister lurking in the shadows, the Arlington House continues to intrigue those seeking answers to its paranormal mysteries.
